From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every material term. Its "[STANDARD]/FINAL/cleared" labels, its "market standard" preamble and its "reviewer efficiency note" do not change our positions. I have reviewed every item, including those marked [STANDARD]. Nothing here is cleared unless it is confirmed through our own authority process, and Amelia Frost's written approval is required for the fallback positions the Seller has adopted.

## 1. Core Liability Terms

| Term | Seller draft | Buyer playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m starting; 20% / AUD 4.8m is a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft (none given) | Seller has adopted our fallback number as its opening position |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher threshold |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, recovery of excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, seller liable from first dollar once exceeded (tipping) | Seller's basket is roughly 5x ours and operates as a deductible |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval (none given) | Fallback adopted without authority |

**Pushback:** Reject all four. Our numbers are the baseline. The Seller's 4.8m cap matching our fallback does not clear it, and the playbook rules out treating a matching number as approval. The preamble's "10–20% / ~1% / 12–18 months" claims are the Seller's assertions and do not bind us.

## 2. Structural Departures

**a) Fundamental / Title and capacity (Seller proposal).** The Seller wants capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits. Our playbook requires a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and no application of the basket, de minimis or buyer-knowledge bar. This is a major departure, and "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept it. **Reject.**

**b) Hidden general-regime override (cl 12/13).** The Seller states that any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise." This would let the general regime override the separate categories (Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant). Our playbook prohibits this. **Reject.** Each category must be expressly separate.

**c) Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).** These apply to "all Claims of any nature" with no fraud carve-out. Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive that carve-out. **Reject** and insert the carve-out in each clause.

**d) Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** The Seller would bar claims for any matter the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge of," including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. Combined with the disclosure regime (see below), this would remove most of our protection. The matters now disclosed in the Disclosure Letter (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006, etc.) are exactly the matters a knowledge bar would neutralise. Our playbook requires deletion of blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. **Reject.**

**e) Disclosure (Schedule 7 and DL 1.1/1.2).** The Seller relies on general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. **Reject.** Note also that DL 1.4 and 11 deny that any consent, payment or notice is legally required. That is a non-admission, so we cannot rely on the Seller's disclosures to confirm what is required. Our own legal analysis is needed.

## 3. Specific Matters

**Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL §2).** Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%). The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours and treating consent as satisfied "on delivery" of the counterparty's consent. The DL confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied. Our playbook requires effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent, and consent-on-delivery is not acceptable. **Reject; make this a condition precedent.**

**Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL §3).** The Seller proposes a release "following Completion" for about AUD 3.2m outstanding. The DL confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included. Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. **Reject.** This is also consistent with our debt-free/cash-free baseline, so the payout should be deducted through the price mechanics. Confirm this with the funds flow.

**Employee bonuses (funds flow; DL §5).** The Seller's funds flow omits the AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses. The Seller describes this as "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised." The DL says the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. Our playbook requires the bonuses, plus triggered on-costs, to be a specific line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them. **Reject.** Require quantification of on-costs.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL §4).** The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment of AUD 180,000 and calls it "adequate." DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. Our playbook requires broadening the narrow indemnity and preserving the SOW3 cure. **Reject.** Verify payment status independently before accepting any figure.

**Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL §6).** The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The DL says the investigation is preliminary, the scope and access are unknown, and whether notification is required is undetermined. Our playbook requires that we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction, while requiring preservation of logs, investigation and updates. **Reject the materiality characterisation.** Neither side's conclusion should be assumed. Require log preservation, a timetable for investigation and regular written updates. Privacy counsel should assess any notification obligations under the applicable law, without assuming one exists.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DL §8).** The Seller describes these as ordinary-course costs. The DL notes that the disclosure does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and that they should be read together for timing and scope. Our playbook requires assessment, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. **Assess, do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence.** Do not seek a deduction automatically.

**Tax and IP (Seller's "settled" position).** The Seller considers these settled under the general regime. Our playbook keeps Tax and IP OPEN and assumes no unlimited liability and no resolution. **Reject.** These remain open categories.

**Title (cl/Sch; DL §10).** The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. The playbook says DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. **Reject as sufficient.** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence, such as ASIC company extract and PPSR searches, and any Seller-side authority documents.

**Mossvale (DL §9) and office lease (DL §7).** The DL says neither document states that consent is required for the share sale, only a restriction on assignment (Mossvale) and a notification obligation (lease). The playbook does not address these directly. **Our own diligence item:** obtain legal analysis of both clauses before accepting "no consent required." Do not rely on the Seller's position.

## 4. Process Points

- **The reviewer efficiency note** asks us to focus only on [OPEN] items and skip [STANDARD] ones. I have not done that. Labels such as "[STANDARD]", "cleared", "FINAL", "agreed at principal level", "pre-cleared" or "not intended to be re-opened" are not accepted as settled. Authority to settle comes only through our authority process, and I have seen none.
- **The Seller's cap, time limit and threshold numbers** should not be treated as concessions. Any movement toward our fallbacks requires Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the specific draft.
- **Facts not verified:** I have not independently confirmed the Riverlark balance, the Ironquay AUD 180,000, the bonus on-costs or the Sandbar renewal terms. These need source verification.

## 5. Summary of Recommendations

1. **Reject the entire Seller package as drafted.** Respond with our mark-up on our baseline positions.
2. **Liability:** restore a 25% / AUD 6.0m general cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 tipping basket, and 24-month general claims period. Use fallbacks only with Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
3. **Fundamental/Title:** separate regime with 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Reject the "same as general" proposal.
4. **No hidden override:** each category stands alone. Reject the "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** add to all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, with no waiver.
6. **Disclosure:** replace whole-data-room, public-register and Accounts deemed disclosure with specific fair disclosure.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete clause 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must not excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions as a pre-Completion condition. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
9. **Riverlark:** current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus quantified on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. No silent exclusion.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, independently verify payment status and obtain a confirmatory assignment.
12. **DD-006:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Reject the "not material" characterisation.
13. **Sandbar:** assess the renewals. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
14. **Tax and IP:** keep open. Reject "settled under general regime."
15. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is insufficient alone.
16. **Mossvale and lease:** obtain legal analysis before accepting the Seller's "no consent required" position.

*This review is based solely on the documents provided and the playbook. It is not a substitute for advice from qualified NSW counsel, and any fallback movement requires the approvals set out above.*
